==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/səˈpɔːt/|[səˈpʰɔːt]|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/səˈpoɹt/|[səˈpʰo̞ɹt]|a=GenAm}}
* {{IPA|en|/səˈpo(ː)ɹt/|a=rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}
* {{IPA|en|/səˈpoət/|a=non-rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)t|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|sup|port}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-support.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-support.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per- (fare)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|supporten}}, from {{der|en|fro|supporter}}, from {{der|en|la|supportō}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{senseid|en|to keep from falling}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To help keep from falling.
#: {{syn|en|bear|bestand|hold up|stut|undergird|underprop|upbear|upgird|uphold|take|bolster}}
#: {{ux|en|Don’t move that beam! It '''supports''' the whole platform.}}
#: {{ux|en|He staggered away from the accident site, '''supported''' by one friend on each side.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1995|author=Nancy Berliner; Sarah Handler|title=Friends of the House|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=3P0MAAAAYAAJ|isbn=0883891344|page=79
|passage=There is a soft-mat seat (which originally had a palm fiber underwebbing) '''supported''' by three curved transverse braces.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2000|journal=Field & Stream|volume=105|number=6|page=87
|passage=One of the keys to glassing effectively is '''supporting''' your binoculars. Advanced glassers who scan lots of country for long periods of time, or who use binoculars of 10X power or more, often use a lightweight camera tripod {{...}}}}
# {{senseid|en|to back a cause, party, etc. mentally or with concrete aid}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To back or favor a cause, party, etc., mentally or with concrete aid:
#: {{syn|en|adhere|}}
#: {{ant|en|oppose}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''support''' France in the World Cup.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[provide]] [[sustenance]] or [[maintenance]] for; to [[sustain]] in [[integrity]] or [[livelihood]].
#: {{ux|en|Mars does not currently '''support''' human habitation.}}
#* {{RQ:Johnson Dictionary|entry={{smallcaps|Oats}}|noformat=1|page=232|column=1|passage=A grain, which in England is generally given to horſes, but which in Scotland '''ſupports''' the people.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To help, particularly financially; to [[subsidize]].
#: {{ux|en|The government '''supports''' the arts in several ways.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Ben Tinker, Meg Tirrell and Brenda Goodman|title=New director named at National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases after Fauci’s retirement|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/08/02/health/niaid-director-jeanne-marrazzo/index.html|date=2023-08-02|passage=The NIAID '''supports''' projects at universities and research organizations around the United States as well as a network of 21 NIAID labs across the country.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260102041825/https://www.cnn.com/2023/08/02/health/niaid-director-jeanne-marrazzo/index.html|archivedate=2 January 2026}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To provide evidence for; to lend [[credibility]] to.
#: {{syn|en|attest|corroborate|establish|substantiate|sustain|verify|undergird}}
#: {{ux|en|The testimony is not sufficient to '''support''' the charges.}}
#: {{ux|en|The evidence will not '''support''' the statements or allegations.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1754|author={{w|Jonathan Edwards (theologian)|Jonathan Edwards}} |title=w:The Freedom of the Will
|passage=to urge such arguments, as though they were sufficient to '''support''' and demonstrate a whole scheme of moral philosophy}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To serve, as in a customer-oriented position; to give support to.
#: {{ux|en|The IT Department '''supports''' the research organization, but not the sales force.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To assist or be involved with, but not be responsible for.
#: {{ux|en|I '''support''' the administrative activities of the executive branch of the organization.}}
#: {{ux|en|I don't make decisions, but I '''support''' those who do.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To answer questions and resolve problems regarding something sold.
#: {{ux|en|Sure they sell the product, but do they '''support''' it?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|software|hardware|said of electronic devices, programming languages, etc.}} To be designed to provide capacity for; to work or be [[compatible]] with (a part, accessory, file type, program, algorithm, etc.).
#: {{syn|en|accommodate|enable|play#Verb|run#Verb}}
#: {{ux|en|Early personal computers did not '''support''' voice-recognition hardware or software.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To [[endure]] without being [[overcome]]; [[bear]]; [[undergo]]; [[tolerate]].
#* {{RQ:Dryden Spanish Fryar
|passage=This fierce demeanour and his insolence / The patience of a god could not '''support'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1881 |author=s:Robert Louis Stevenson |title=s:Virginibus Puerisque
|passage=For a strong affection such moments are worth '''supporting''', and they will end well; for your advocate is in your lover's heart and speaks her own language{{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To play a lesser [[part#noun|part]] in the same production with (a star performer).
#: {{ux|en|to '''support''' the character of King Lear}}
#: {{ux|en|And the award for best '''supporting''' actress goes to...}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|support}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|frm|support}}. Displaced {{noncog|ang|wraþu}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|agent}}{{lb|en|sometimes|attributive}} Something which supports.
#: {{syn|en|[[sustentation]] (formal)}}
#: {{ux|en|Don't move that beam! It's a '''support''' for the whole platform.}}
# {{senseid|en|help}} Financial or other help.
#: {{ux|en|The government provides '''support''' to the arts in several ways.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=December 19, 2011|author=Kerry Brown| title=Kim Jong-il obituary| url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2011/dec/19/kim-jong-il| passage=Kim was educated at the newly founded university in Pyongyang, named after his father, graduating in 1964. The 1960s and early 1970s were the golden years for the DPRK. It undertook rapid industrialisation, economically outstripped its southern competitor, and enjoyed the '''support''' of both the People's Republic of China, and the Soviet Union.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011190910/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/dec/19/kim-jong-il|archivedate=11 October 2026}}
# {{senseid|en|answers}} Answers to questions and resolution of problems regarding something sold.
#: {{hypo|en|first-level support|second-level support|third-level support}}
#: {{ux|en|Sure they sell the product, but do they provide '''support'''?}}
# {{senseid|en|function}} {{lb|en|mathematics|in relation to a [[function]]}} the set of [[point]]s where the function is not zero; the [[closure]] of that set.
#: {{ant|en|kernel}}
# {{senseid|en|fuzzy}} {{lb|en|fuzzy set theory}} A set whose elements are at least partially included in a given [[fuzzy set]] (i.e., whose grade of membership in that fuzzy set is strictly greater than zero).
#: {{ux|en|If the membership function of a fuzzy set is continuous, then that fuzzy set's '''support''' is an open set.}}
# {{senseid|en|prime}} {{c|en|Algebra}}{{lb|en|[[commutative algebra]]|of a module <math>M</math> over a commutative [[ring]] <math>R</math>}} The set of all [[prime ideal]]s of <math>R</math> such that the [[localization]] of <math>M</math> at the prime is nonzero, denoted <math>\operatorname{Supp} M</math>
# {{senseid|en|evidence}} Evidence.
#: {{ux|en|The new research provides further '''support''' for our theory.}}
# {{senseid|en|compatibility}} {{lb|en|software|hardware}} [[compatibility|Compatibility]] and [[functionality]] for a given product or feature.
#: {{ux|en|This game has no mouse '''support'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|cinema}} {{lb|en|cinema}} An [[actor]] playing a [[subordinate]] part with a [[star]].
# {{senseid|en|accompaniment}} {{lb|en|music}} An [[accompaniment]] in [[music]].
# {{senseid|en|support position}} {{lb|en|gymnastics}} {{clipping of|en|support position}}.
# {{senseid|en|movable}} {{lb|en|structural analysis}} Horizontal, vertical or rotational support of [[structures]]: [[movable]], [[hinged]], [[fixed]]. {{rfex|en}}
